To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
repair activities in Dhaka's markets reveal forms of craft-based innovation, embedded in global flows, that cast new light on the problems of learning and sustainable design.

1) Repair work is embedded in global networks of repair and reuse that are sustained by local repairers, 2) Repair work in Dhaka is a form of craft-based innovation that involves both the reuse of existing components and the creation of new components, and 3) Repair work is an important form of learning for repairers and their customers.

repair work is a site of craft-based knowledge production and innovation, and that taking repair work more seriously can cast new and useful light on the problems of learning and sustainable development in the design and use of interactive systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the ways in which repair work is an important and often overlooked aspect of interactive systems, and how understanding the nature and role of repair in such systems can shed new light on a series of HCI concerns.
the ways in which repair activities are implicated in processes of learning and innovation in interactive systems, and how such processes might be supported by design.
how repair activities can inform our understanding of learning, innovation and sustainability in HCI.

the repair of mobile phones is a very important activity in Bangladesh.
repair is a key element of the innovation system, and it is a key element in the sustainability of the system, and it can be a key element in learning in the system.
repair work is an important and often overlooked form of innovation, learning, maintenance, and sustainability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
repair is a critical activity for understanding and designing interactive technologies.
repair is an important site of learning and innovation, and that repair work is an integral part of the life cycle of complex interactive technologies.
repair work can provide a new lens on innovation, learning, sustainability, and other core HCI concerns.

repair work, in the form of acts of maintenance and repair, can provide fresh insight on innovation, learning and sustainability in interactive system research and design.
repair work is an important and underappreciated source of innovation, learning, adaptation, and resilience in the operation of interactive systems.
repair activities in the global South are a critical and often overlooked site of innovation, knowledge, and sustainability.
